summary: Dependency-confusion recon beacon exfiltrates host identifiers to hardcoded bare-IP endpoint
details: Package published under the @ecg-internal scope ships a postinstall script `node beacon.cjs` and a stub `index.js` that both POST installer identifiers to a hardcoded bare-IP destination over cleartext HTTP: `http://185.158.107.175:8787/_ah/dc`. The beacon payload includes `os.hostname()`, the absolute install path (`__dirname`), `process.cwd()`, and `process.version`, labeled as the package name. The beacon fires automatically on `npm install` via the declared postinstall lifecycle hook and additionally on `require()` of the module. The shipped `index.js` is a Proxy of no-op functions presented as a 'Compatibility shim.', so a build that resolves this public package in place of a private internal `@ecg-internal/aurora-js-formatters` succeeds silently while reporting the successful install to the operator of 185.158.107.175. The scope naming, cleartext bare-IP destination unrelated to any declared publisher infrastructure, and the hollow Proxy export are the dependency-confusion recon-callback shape.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
